T: Something big is cooking in Chinatown.
D: A loudmouth truck driver gets dragged into a magical underworld battle in San Francisco's Chinatown.
P: Serve the ribs when Jack drives the Pork-Chop Express into Chinatown.
S: Wang's family restaurant, before everything goes sideways
Mix pork mince with garlic chives, ginger, soy, Shaoxing and sesame oil, pleat into gyoza wrappers. Pan-fry until the bottoms crisp, add water, lid on for 4 minutes. Black vinegar and chilli oil dip.
Score squid, cut into strips, toss in potato starch with salt, white pepper and five spice, fry at 190C for 90 seconds. Wok-toss with fried garlic, sliced chilli and spring onion.
the Chinatown kitchen where it all starts
Pork, cabbage and mushroom rolled in spring roll wrappers, fried at 180C until crisp, sweet chilli and soy for dipping.
M: Pork ribs rubbed with hoisin, honey, soy, five spice, red fermented bean curd and garlic overnight. Roast at 160C covered for 90 minutes, uncover, glaze and blast at 220C until sticky and charred.
Fry pork mince with ya cai and Sichuan pepper until crisp. Sauce of sesame paste, chilli oil, black vinegar and soy in the bowl, thin wheat noodles on top, then the pork and spring onion.
W: Whisk egg whites, sugar, flour, melted butter and vanilla to a thin batter, spread 8cm circles, bake at 180C for 6 minutes, fold around a paper fortune while hot.
K: Egg Shen's bottle for the trip below Chinatown

Plum wine shaken with lemon, ginger syrup and egg white, served over ice with a pickled plum or a cherry. Simmer 50g sugar, 50ml water and 20g sliced ginger for 5 minutes, then cool and strain. Shake 240ml plum wine, 60ml lemon juice, 40ml ginger syrup and 1 egg white without ice for 15 seconds, then with ice for 15 seconds. Strain into 4 ice-filled glasses and garnish with a pickled plum or cherry.

dishes.make_ahead: Fry the crisp pork up to 2 days ahead, keep chilled and reheat in the wok; mix the sauce in the bowls and cook the noodles on the night

steps.text: Put a large pot of water on to boil. Slice the spring onions and rinse and chop the mustard greens.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok and fry the pork mince with the mustard greens and Sichuan pepper over high heat for 8 minutes until crisp and dry.
Divide the sesame paste, chilli oil, black vinegar and soy sauce between four bowls and stir each with 2 tbsp of the hot water.
Cook the wheat noodles for 2 to 3 minutes, drain and pile on top of the sauce.
Spoon over the crisp pork, scatter with spring onion and toss at the table.

veg.n: Wang Chi's dan dan noodles with crisp mushroom
veg.make_ahead: Fry the crisp mushroom and tofu up to 2 days ahead, keep chilled and reheat in the wok; mix the sauce in the bowls and cook the noodles on the night

steps.text: Put a large pot of water on to boil. Slice the spring onions, rinse and chop the mustard greens, finely chop the mushrooms and crumble the tofu.

Heat the vegetable oil in a wok and fry the mushrooms and tofu over high heat for 12 minutes until dry and browning. Add the mustard greens, Sichuan pepper and 1 tbsp of the soy sauce and fry 2 minutes more until crisp.
Divide the sesame paste, chilli oil, black vinegar and remaining soy sauce between four bowls and stir each with 2 tbsp of the hot water.
Cook the wheat noodles for 2 to 3 minutes, drain and pile on top of the sauce.
Spoon over the crisp mushroom, scatter with spring onion and toss at the table.
Mix the hoisin, honey, soy, five spice, bean curd and garlic and rub over the ribs.
Marinate in the fridge overnight, at least 8 hours.
Roast covered at 160C.
Uncover, glaze and blast at 220C until sticky.
Rest briefly before serving.

veg.n: Pork-Chop Express char siu mushroom ribs

steps.text: Score the cut side of the king oyster mushrooms in a criss-cross. Mash the hoisin, honey, soy, five spice, bean curd, garlic and oil together and rub over the mushrooms, keeping a few spoonfuls back for glazing.
Marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours, overnight is better.
Lay the mushrooms cut side up in a roasting tin, cover with foil and roast at 180C.
Uncover, brush with the saved glaze and blast at 220C until sticky and charred at the edges.
Rest for a few minutes before serving.
Whisk the egg whites with the sugar, then stir in the flour, butter and vanilla.
Spread 8cm circles on a lined tray, a few at a time.
Bake at 180C.
Working fast, fold each around a paper fortune while hot.

s.note: Crisp-bottomed pork and chive dumplings with vinegar and chilli oil
s.how: Mix 400g pork mince with a chopped bunch of garlic chives, 1 tbsp grated ginger, 1 tbsp soy, 1 tbsp Shaoxing and 1 tsp sesame oil. Pleat into 30 gyoza wrappers. Fry until the bottoms crisp, add water and steam with the lid on for 4 minutes.

s.note: Crisp squid tossed with fried garlic, chilli and spring onion
s.how: Score 500g squid tubes and cut into strips. Toss in 100g potato starch with salt, white pepper and a pinch of five spice. Fry at 190C for 90 seconds. Wok-toss with fried garlic, 2 sliced chillies and spring onion.

m.note: Sticky charred five spice ribs, glazed in hoisin and honey
m.how: Rub 1.5kg pork ribs with 4 tbsp hoisin, 2 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp soy, 1 tsp five spice, 1 cube red fermented bean curd and 3 garlic cloves. Marinate overnight. Roast covered at 160C for 90 minutes, then uncover, glaze and blast at 220C until sticky.

w.note: Crisp vanilla fortune cookies, each with a paper fortune inside
w.how: Whisk 3 egg whites with 100g sugar, then stir in 60g flour, 40g melted butter and a little vanilla. Spread 8cm circles on a lined tray and bake at 180C for 6 minutes. Working fast, fold each around a paper fortune while hot.

d.note: Plum wine shaken with lemon, ginger syrup and egg white, served over ice with a pickled plum or a cherry.
d.how: Simmer 50g sugar, 50ml water and 20g sliced ginger for 5 minutes, then cool and strain. Shake 240ml plum wine, 60ml lemon juice, 40ml ginger syrup and 1 egg white without ice for 15 seconds, then with ice for 15 seconds. Strain into 4 ice-filled glasses and garnish with a pickled plum or cherry.
